new_statements.quote: ACCENT D'INTENSITE. Cet accent porte en général sur la première syllabe de la racine. Dans le cas d'un radical de plus de trois syllabes un accent secondaire affecte également la pénultième. Un radical monosyllabique reporte l'accent sur le préfixe de classe. L'accent d'intensité est, au reste, assez peu prononcé. Il importe de ne pas l'exagérer ni de le transformer en accent de hauteur.
new_statements.translation: STRESS ACCENT. This accent generally falls on the first syllable of the root. In the case of a radical of more than three syllables a secondary accent also affects the penultimate. A monosyllabic radical shifts the accent onto the class prefix. The stress accent is, moreover, rather weakly marked. One must not exaggerate it nor turn it into a pitch accent.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Weak dynamic stress on the root-initial (stem-initial) syllable of the word; if the root is monosyllabic the stress retracts onto the noun-class prefix; the language is otherwise tonal (H vs L, plus rising/falling), tone being treated separately under 'Tonologie / accent de hauteur'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: In radicals of more than three syllables a secondary accent falls on the penultimate syllable (Bennett 1978 apud Hyman 2009: 203 summarises this as 'stem stress with secondary penultimate stress').
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic radicals: accent moves to the class prefix. Author stresses the accent is weak ('assez peu prononcé'). No lexical exceptions mentioned in the visible text.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (root + prefix) statement in a grammar whose prosodic marking is otherwise tonal; identical wording to Mamet 1955: 11 for the sister language Ntomba C35a (quoted by Hyman 2009: 201). The 1962 Aequatoria review warns Mamet's Bolia data are partly from Ntomba-influenced informants gathered near Bikoro, outside Bolia country.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement is for Bolia proper (lolia, Guthrie C35b, boli1255) as described by Mamet 1960; the 1962 Aequatoria review (signed E. S.) cautions that Mamet's material came partly from Ntomba-speaking or Ntomba-influenced informants near Bikoro, and the accent paragraph is word-for-word the same as Mamet 1955: 11 for Ntomba (ntom1248, C35a). Not to be confused with the aequatoria.be index entry 'dialect der Bolia' (= Boyela, Hulstaert 1942).
